title: Assistant Professor of Economics
description:
Salary:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of
the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through
the internal application process.

Job Category:Faculty

Employment Type:Regular

Job Profile:Assistant Professor

Job Summary:

The highly ranked Department of Economics is seeking excellent
candidates for a tenure-track faculty position. We welcome
applications from scholars in any field of economics. Fields
currently represented in the Department include, but are not
limited to, Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and Monetary Economics,
Mathematical and Quantitative Economics (including Econometrics),
International Economics, Public Economics, Labor Economics,
Economic Development, and Industrial Organization.

The successful candidate will conduct and publish independent
scholarly research in nationally and internationally recognized
outlets through a research agenda that contributes to the analysis
of market-based solutions to societal challenges, as described
under Qualifications.

The successful candidate, as a member of the College of L&S,
will proactively contribute to, support, and advance the college’s
commitment to excellence among all aspects of their teaching,
mentoring, research, and service; which includes making significant
contributions to the department’s teaching mission through course
development and delivery to undergraduate and graduate students in
one or more fields of economics specialization. The general
teaching load is 2 courses per year, 1 in one semester and 1 in the
other.

In keeping with the college’s educational mission that prioritizes
and actualizes evidence-based and student-centered teaching and
(undergraduate student) mentoring, successful applicants will
supervise and mentor graduate students, including thesis and
dissertation research; contribute to the development of Department
programs and serve on departmental committees; and participate in
the academic and administrative affairs of the Department and in
university, professional, national, and international service as
appropriate to rank.

The successful candidate will engage in the intellectual life of
the Department through scholarly research, teaching at the
undergraduate and graduate levels, graduate student mentoring and
supervision, and university and professional service. The
Department values open inquiry, rigorous debate, and scholarly
engagement with competing explanations and institutional
approaches.

The Department of Economics at UW-Madison is highly rated and is a
leader in its field, generally ranked in the top 15 economics
departments in the nation. Our department is multidisciplinary and
has a highly collaborative environment. Madison is the state's
capitol city and is well known for offering a small town feel in a
medium sized city. It is a great place to raise a family and offers
an ideal combination of natural beauty, stimulating cultural
events, outstanding schools and outdoor recreation.

In the College of Letters & Science, we provide a liberal arts
education that is both broad and deep through excellent, empathic
teaching. We hire faculty who are interested in pursuing difficult
questions, making new discoveries, and making an impact in their
field. We reward excellent teaching and classroom innovation, and
we are committed to shared governance. Learn more about the L&S
mission on our webpage: https://ls.wisc.edu/about/mission .

Key Job Responsibilities:

Conduct and publish independent scholarly research in nationally
and internationally recognized outlets through a research agenda
that contributes to the analysis of market-based solutions to
societal challenges

Participate in the academic and administrative affairs of the
Department and in university, professional, national, and
international service as appropriate to rank

Contributions to course development and delivery for undergraduates
and graduates.

Supervise and mentor graduate students, including thesis and
dissertation research

Proactively contribute to, support, and advance the college’s
commitment to excellence among all aspects of their teaching,
mentoring, research, and service.

Contribute to the development of Department programs and serve on
departmental committees

Department:

College of Letters and Science - Department of Economics

Compensation:

Negotiable – 9 months / ongoing / renewable

Required Qualifications:

This position is part of a university initiative to broaden the
range of scholarly perspectives represented on campus. The search
is broad with respect to field and methodology, while focused on
research that takes market institutions, competition, incentives,
or alternative institutional arrangements as central objects of
analysis in addressing societal challenges. Relevant topics include
but are not limited to: competition and market power; property
rights and contracting; entrepreneurship and innovation; the
design, effects, and limits of regulation; institutional and
mechanism design; decentralized information and price formation;
and market-based approaches to policy problems.

Applicants should have research underway that demonstrates the
potential to produce high-quality publications and make a lasting
impact in their field of specialization and should demonstrate the
potential for excellence in teaching at the undergraduate and
graduate levels. In addition, the successful candidate will
demonstrate fostering or the ability to foster a teaching,
learning, mentoring, departmental, and research environment where
all can thrive.

The successful candidate will advance the educational mission of
the College of Letters & Science that values, prioritizes, and
actualizes evidence-based and student-centered teaching and
(undergraduate student) mentoring. They will contribute to an
environment that fosters engagement and a sense of belonging for
faculty, staff, students and members of the broader
community.

Education:

A PhD in economics required by start of appointment.

How to Apply:

Please note that applicants will be evaluated based upon submitted
application materials and therefore should speak to and include
evidence of their qualifications. Application materials must
clearly demonstrate the applicant’s dedication to excellence in
student-centered teaching and mentoring. Additionally, materials
should showcase the applicant’s ability to purposefully plan their
teaching practices, evidenced through goals, action plans,
reflection, and related documentation. This portion of the
application materials must be created by the applicant and may
include supporting letters. It cannot be only in the form of
letters and testimony by others.

Apply online at "Jobs at UW" (http://jobs.wisc.edu) under Job
Requisition JR10014688. Applications must be received through UW-
Madison's online application system. Applications submitted outside
of this system will not be considered. Click the "" button to start
the application process. Applicants should submit the following 4
items:

a letter of application

curriculum vitae

a combined research, teaching, and mentoring statement

a job market paper


All applicants will receive an email after their application is
submitted asking them to provide the name and contact information
for three references, and each reference will receive an electronic
link through which they can upload a signed letter of
reference.

For full consideration, all materials must be received no later
than 11:59 p.m. on November 15th, 2026. Applications received after
that date may be considered until position is filled. Please note
that applicants will be evaluated based upon submitted application
materials and therefore should speak to and include evidence of
their qualifications.

The University of Wisconsin-Madison fulfills its public mission by

background - people who as students, faculty, and staff serve

The University of Wisconsin-Madison is an Equal Opportunity
